title: Beach-Hopping in Albania by Car: 3-Day Himarë‑Ksamil Route
excerpt: Discover a compact 3‑day coastal road trip from Himarë to Ksamil, hopping iconic beaches, hidden coves, and practical driving tips with a rental car from Tiran…
intro: The Albanian Riviera offers a seamless blend of turquoise waters, rugged cliffs, and sun‑kissed sands. With a reliable rental from AutoConnect at Tirana Rinas Airport, you can embark on a relaxed 3‑day adventure that strings together the region’s most beautiful beaches without feeling rushed.

sections.title: Beach-Hopping in Albania by Car: Day 1 – Himarë to Porto Palermo
sections.body: After picking up your car at Tirana Airport, drive the 220 km coastal stretch to Himarë (about 4 hours). Park near the town centre and head east along the SH8 to Porto Palermo, a short 15‑minute detour. The bay’s calm, crystal‑clear water is perfect for a quick dip, and the 16th‑century castle provides a scenic backdrop for photos. Allow 2–3 hours for swimming, a light lunch at a waterfront café, and a leisurely stroll before returning to Himarë for the night.

sections.title: Day 2 – Borsh, Gjipe Canyon & Bunec Coves
sections.body: Start early and follow SH8 south to Borsh, Albania’s longest beach (7 km). Spend the morning sunbathing or walking the shoreline; the sand is soft and the sea is inviting. Continue to Gjipe Canyon, where a short hike leads to a hidden pebble beach—parking is limited, so a quick walk from the lot is required. In the afternoon, drive a few kilometres further to the secluded Bunec coves, accessible via a narrow, paved lane that ends at a modest parking area. Pack water and snacks, as facilities are sparse.

sections.title: Day 3 – Sarandë, Ksamil & the Blue Lagoon
sections.body: The final day begins with a brief stop in Sarandë, a lively town where you can explore the promenade and enjoy a coffee with a view of the Ionian Sea. From there, the 12 km drive to Ksamil is straightforward; follow signs to the popular beach cluster near the Greek border. Ksamil’s white‑sand beaches and shallow waters are ideal for families, but summer parking fills quickly—arrive early or use the municipal lot on the outskirts. End the day with a sunset swim at the nearby Blue Lagoon before heading back to your rental.

sections.title: Practical Driving Tips for the Southern Coast
sections.body: The SH8 highway is fully asphalted and well‑maintained, yet some access roads to hidden coves are steep and narrow; a compact car with good ground clearance is sufficient—no 4x4 needed. Fill up on fuel in Himarë or Sarandë, as stations become scarce further south. Keep change handy for parking meters in Ksamil during peak season. Use the car’s GPS or a reliable offline map, and respect local speed limits (50 km/h in villages, 80 km/h on the main coastal road).

tip.title: Pro Tip: Reserve a GPS‑Equipped Compact Car
tip.body: Booking a compact model with an integrated GPS through AutoConnect ensures easy navigation on the winding SH8 and helps you locate the small parking lots that serve the hidden beaches.

faq.question: How long does it take to drive from Himarë to Ksamil?
faq.answer: The direct drive along SH8 covers about 65 km and takes roughly 1.5 to 2 hours, but adding beach stops will extend the travel time to 3–4 hours.

faq.question: Are the coastal roads in southern Albania safe for a rental car?
faq.answer: Yes, the main SH8 route is fully paved and regularly maintained. Only the short access roads to secluded coves are narrow, but a standard rental car handles them comfortably.

faq.question: Can you access secret beaches in the Albanian Riviera without a 4x4?
faq.answer: Most hidden spots, such as Bunec and Gjipe, are reachable by a regular compact car; you may need to park and walk a short distance, but a 4x4 is not required.
